steps.prompt: A $2$ m pole casts a $3$ m shadow. At the same moment a tree casts a $15$ m shadow. How tall is the tree?

cards.title: Same shape, different size
cards.body: Similar triangles have the same angles, and their matching sides are all in the same ratio. Two equal angles are enough to prove it (AA). A line parallel to one side of a triangle cuts off a smaller triangle similar to the whole.

cards.title: Worked example: a parallel cut
cards.problem: In triangle $ABC$, $DE$ is parallel to $BC$ with $D$ on $AB$ and $E$ on $AC$. $AD = 4$, $DB = 6$ and $DE = 5$. How long is $BC$?

cards.title: Scaling areas
cards.body: If every length is multiplied by $k$, every area is multiplied by $k^2$ (and every volume by $k^3$). In a right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse makes two smaller triangles similar to the whole: the altitude $h$ and the two pieces $p$, $q$ of the hypotenuse satisfy $h^2 = pq$.

cards.title: Worked example: areas
cards.problem: Two similar triangles have sides in the ratio $2 : 3$. The smaller has area $12$. What is the area of the larger?

try.prompt: By what fraction are the areas multiplied?
What is the area of the larger triangle?

cards.title: The common trap: mismatched sides
cards.body: Match the sides that face equal angles. With a parallel cut, compare the small triangle with the WHOLE triangle ($AB$, not $DB$). And areas scale by the square of the ratio, not by the ratio.

prompts: How do you make sure you are matching the right sides of two similar triangles?
